key_insight: A parameterized physics-informed neural network predicts embedded microchannel cooling across a continuous geometric design space, with reported simulation speedups exceeding four orders of magnitude.
engineering_relevance: The surrogate could accelerate the design and optimization of embedded liquid cooling for high-performance electronic chips.
method: Inputs combine four geometric dimensions with three spatial coordinates to predict thermohydraulic fields.
Training combines geometric ansatz embedding, SOAP optimization, and a thermal-conductivity-based curriculum.
An optimized JAX backend enables convergence in under four hours on a single consumer-grade GPU.
evidence_signal: Against finite-element simulations, the abstract reports relative errors of 8.1% for velocity fields and 5.6% for temperature fields.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify validation coverage across the design space or reliability beyond the trained geometric range.
paper_title: Parameterized Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Efficient Simulation of Embedded Microfluidic Chip Cooling
